reviewText: I really want to give this watch a 5 star rating, but I can't do it.  It may not be fair that I have a Nokia Windows Phone and Pebble does not support Windows phones, but I'm taking that into account and if I was rating on functionality, I would give it a 2 star rating.  The problem is both with Pebble and Microsoft.  I want a smart watch, but due to security limitations with WP8, we may never see a fully functioning smart watch for WP8.  The Pebble seemed to be the most promising with 2 apps that support some functionality.The reason Windows Phone 8 won't work with Pebble or other smart watches:- Microsoft will not allow SMS messages or Phone calls to be intercepted by any 3rd party app.  One Microsoft employee stated on a forum that this was a problem with Android's security model and to protect the privacy of WP8 users, they will not allow access to these API's (even if a phone user want's to grant this permission).  Also, WP8 doesn't really have background applications.  It has a scheduling agent that allows apps limited functionality to do some tasks periodically.- Pebble will not release the low level communication protocol for the bluetooth endpoints.  This limits developers to using the libraries Pebble develops (currently only iOS and Android).  A couple developers reverse engineered the protocol and were able to create two apps, but they are very limited.What can you do with WP8 and Pebble (if you pay $3 for two apps):- Update firmware.- Install watch faces and apps.- Get calendar notifications (only if lock screen is disabled and app is running).- Control Music (lock screen disabled, app running)- Twitter feeds (lock screen disabled, app running)- Phone battery status (lock screen disabled, app running)- Update time- Network alerts (lock screen disabled, app running)- Send some sample notifications, if someday Microsoft opens the SMS and Phone notifications.Pros with the watch:- I think it looks elegant.  It's not as big and bulky as it looks in the pictures.- I like the ability to change my watch face.- The backlight works well and with a flick of the wrist.- It's faster than I expected, probably because I was expecting e-ink, like the Kindle (this is not e-ink).  e-ink is very slow to refresh and this is fast because it is really an LCD screen.  e-Paper is a technology that is very low power and easy to read without a back light, but it is not the same as e-ink.- It's more sturdy than I expected for a plastic watch.Cons with the watch:- The buttons are a little hard to push and feel clunky.- I was expecting e-ink.  I'm not that disappointed, e-paper is faster.- It's a little difficult to navigate the watch, probably because the buttons are hard to push.- It only holds 8 apps/watchfaces- Not an open development framework.  Development is very tightly controlled, it appears.- Straps are actually attractive, but not what you would expect for a $150 watch.- Charging cable is magnetic, but still needs to be tinkered with to make sure it is aligned.

reviewText: I am pleased with this purchase. The watch performs as advertised after setup. The camo band is understated, which I like. That is to say that it is unquestionably camo, but it does not attract attention as such like, say having every possible camo truck accesory or having a camo recliner in your living room might, if you know what I mean. The watch is a bit larger than I usually prefer, but it is not too large so as to be uncomfortable or attract too much attention. I have a medium/small wrist and fortunately the band fits without extending past the point where the elastic retainer can hold it. So far the rotating bezel has stayed put all but once, when it moved about 15 degrees - likely from going in and out of a pocket multiple times.The key here for me was to have a durable multi-function watch with the compass/alt/barometer functions that is cool looking but doesn't exist purely as a techie or outdoorsman status symbol. This watch was a bit more expensive than some other options, but I wanted a solar powered one that was perhaps a bit less obvious on the wrist than some other options. I actually enjoy and use the moon phase display quite a bit for some reason. The backlight illuminates the entire face and all aspects of the display are readable.In all I reccomend the watch if it falls in your price range. Casio makes a much less expensive model (SGW300HB-3AVCF) that runs on batteries and is not atomic that I would suggest if you wish to have similar features under $75 and don't mind tons of lettering on your wrist. That said, this watch is much much cooler looking, understated, and solar powered...

description: It's no longer enough to train hard; you also have to train smart if you want an edge. Enter the Timex Ironman 150-Lap Sleek watch, which gives you the edge when every second counts. The watch also offers a 100-hour chronograph with lap and split times, along with a 150-lap memory recall. And that's just the start of the watch's built-in training features, which also include a target time pacer, on-the-fly lap or split recalls, a 199-lap counter, 16 interval timers with repeat, hydration and nutrition alarms, and an automatic interval repetition counter.The 150-Lap Sleek offers non-training functions, too, with three daily, weekly, weekday, or weekend alarms, a 24-hour time display, and month, day, and date displays. reviewText: I've had this watch for several years now and it still holds up. It is a little pricier than some of the competition from Casio and Timex. However, it offers some nice advantages over most others, with only a couple drawbacks. I wore mine for two tours in Iraq and it performed perfectly. Not that I truly ever relied on the Comp-Baro-Alti features, because we always had other more advanced devices for that. But it was reassuring to have those capabilities on my wrist at all times. And the basic time, stopwatch, alarm and timer functions were used often and performed well.Pros:User replaceable battery - very helpful in the field and easy to do, saves money.Broad array of functions - easy to manipulate the various features with a little practice and reading the manual.Very accurate - the watch loses very little time over the months and years, good quartz movement.Good water resistance - not a dive watch, but it holds up well, even under several meters of water, which I've done.Comfortable despite its large size - pretty light weight and a large, comfortable band.Easy to read - large face, big numbers.Attractive design - very distinct look.Cons:Not solar-atomic (like Casio Pathfinder) - however, battery is easily replaced and the quartz movement is very accurate.Thicker case - more so than the Casio PAW1300, but not too bad.Bottonology - the button function layout is different than most Timex and Casios, but isn't too hard to figure out.Price - higher than many, but not excessive for what you get.Overall, despite the drawbacks referenced above, I highly recommend the Suunto X-Lander and I would assume the other Suunto models are also good. Serves me well.
title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: Dunno why they play so coy with the sizing on amazon, but here's what the label on the product says:MENS;L - 7/8XL - 9/10XXL - 11/123XL - 13/11 (I'm guessing they probably meant 13/14 but that's what it says...)WOMENS;S - 5/6M - 7/8L - 9/10XL - 11YOUTHS;YS - 10/11YM - 12/13YL - 1/2S - 3/4M - 5/6I have 9.5 so I got the XL.  There's the physical SENSATION of having no room, but if I actually push my heel back into it, I have a normal amount of wiggle room for a 9.5 shoe.  By virtue of the materials and how it is built, your foot, unlike with a laced-up rigid shoe, migrates to the center of the boot and the cushy material expands to fill all gaps - probably not a bad thing if you want something that will be form-fitting to your foot anyway but if you think that sensation of being in contact with the boot on all sides of your foot might bug you, you might go a size larger.  I imagine if you just sit with your feet up on a coffee table or something reading a book for awhile it will compress the insulation in the back of the heel enough to give the toes a little more wiggle room.  In fairness to the manufacturer, the lower of the two drawstrings appears to be an attempt at a solution to the problem as well - tightening it will pull your foot back towards the heel and give your toes a little more room.  I'd say that all by itself is about a 50% solution for people who dislike the encased feeling on their toes.As far as the rubber stuff on the bottom goes - looks real attractive in its brand new state.  From the other reviews, sounds like it is going to wear off pretty quickly.  One word of advice here folks - SHOE GOO IS YOUR FRIEND.  You ought to have a tube in your junk drawer.  If not, go get some.  Now!  Are you the type that also has no duct tape or wd40 in the house?  What were you thinking!?!?  Rectify the situation ASAP...  Or order it with these booties.  I have some old running shoes that literally fell apart that I glued back together and while they're now just shoes I quickly pull on to grab the paper, go to the mailbox, etc they are definitely not coming apart again in my lifetime.  If you start to see fraying on these booties - shoe goo the stitching areas.  If you start to lose traction, you could shoe goo the entire sole - which would also waterproof it.  If you plan to go this route, lay up a supply of tongue depressors and toothpicks for application before you start - you'll see what I mean.So shoe goo is going to be my future traction solution - either that or maybe the stick-on stuff they sell at the hardware store for ladder rungs, icy steps and the like.  Or maybe the stick-on stuff used to provide traction in bathtubs.  Basically it should not be hard for those of us with hardwood floors to find ways & means of not cracking our skulls.I could see how the sole could compress down over time and you'd end up wanting to replace these... and at around $35 per pair why not, but one other way to go would be to add an insulated insole.  If you want to go really crazy, hilariously enough, I ran across a product here on amazon - heated insoles with a remote controller keychain fob.  I'm not ready for that level of awesomeness yet - but maybe later...I spend a lot of time working in front of a computer in my basement which has tile flooring, so these boots are great for the winter if you like to keep your thermostat down.  I haven't had a chance to take them camping yet, but keeping feet warm in a mummy bag always was a problem for me - I came up with a solution, which was: polypro sock liner, wool sock, huge wool sock, but I could see these booties being an even better solution.  For anyone who gets cold in their mummy bag - you may also want to look into expedition-weight long underwear.  I found some thick polypropylene uppers and lowers awhile back that are super toasty.  Personally I prefer a subpar sleeping bag while wearing warm clothing to an awesome sleeping bag - if you have to get up in the middle of the night or when you get up in the morning, you're still wearing half your insulation.  So in my opinion it's better to upgrade your clothing layers before upgrading your sleeping bag.  Just my two cents.  It's pretty cool these booties have a reasonably tough sole so I won't have to screw around with hunting around in the dark for my boots, pulling off socks, stuffing my feet into a cold pair of boots, and lacing up if nature calls in the middle of the night.  Clearly, too onerous of a task when out there roughing it!  Camping is all about maintaining the highest possible level of comfort, am I right?...but anyway, supercool product.  Dunno why anyone uses normal house slippers when these moonboot thingys are available.  4 instead of 5 stars due to the issue with the manufacturer's rubber material on the soles.  However a little time and a few dollars (a tube of shoe goo is maybe $3) you can soup it up into an even nicer product without too much trouble.  Considering there are other booties out there for $75 or more, doing the extra touches yourself isn't too awful a prospect, so I chose this product over the more expensive (possibly slightly better engineered?) products.
summary: A slightly flawed easily upgraded supercool product

reviewText: Nowadays, when my phone rings, my wrist buzzes. When someone texts me, I don't look at my phone to find out what they said; I look at my watch. Why? I've got a Pebble - the "smartwatch." Pebble describes it as an "E-paper watch for iPhone and Android". The "e-paper" bit might get some thinking you're going to be reading books on it. You're definitely not, but it is a great display. So what do you get for your money? It's a watch, to start with. The face is 144x168 pixels, a large black/white e-paper display. I chose the black body and strap (you can get it in black, white, cherry red or grey). Open the box, and you're instructed to go to getpebble.com. That's a neat touch - no manual at all. The whole initial setup is done through its web page and then app. Open that page on your smartphone, and it directs you to the iPhone or Android app store, where you download a free app which connects via Bluetooth. Through that, you can send software updates (such as new watchfaces) and, more usefully, back-and-forth notifications when someone calls or texts. (You can also set it to notify you when you get an email. Don't do this unless you never get email.) The watchface is scratch-resistant (not -proof) and has an anti-glare coat; I find it very readable in all lights, except when it's dark. Then you have the options of an automatic backlight (adjusted to light levels), or being able to flick your wrist to activate the backlight. The strap feels like rubber; it's wide (to go with the watch) but not uncomfortable. Charging is via a USB lead terminating in a magnetic attachment to a pair of contacts on the left-hand side of the watch; I assume a micro-USB slot would have taken up too much internal space and created waterproofing problems (it is waterproof, at least for swimming). So don't lose that charger; you'll be needing it every four or five days (in my experience, though the makers claim up to seven.. probably if you have Bluetooth off) and it's unique. One bad thing: the interface doesn't show the battery level (even in the phone app), which can leave you in the lurch without warning. The charge level only shows when you're charging, and even then only in the menu, as opposed to standard watch, display.
summary: The Pebble Samrtwatch: "the watch that does what you need."

reviewText: I'm an Android user, and I've had the Pebble Watch for a month now, so I figured I'd leave my thoughts on it here. This watch has its good and its bad, just as any product does; several factors keep me from giving this a 5-star rating.Cons:- Most features that you see on the on [...] (where I got my pebble from) require a third party app, and they don't tell you which. I wish they had provided a list, or integrated options into their own app.- The default app only lets you download some basic watch faces (see above for additional features).- Watch face easily scratches; great for the office environment, but don't tinker around with it.- Better support under Android than iOs, mainly due to phone policies on apps talking to each other (sorry, iPhone users). Fix would be to integrate everything into a single app.Pros:- Once you get the apps installed, you can do some great stuff.- Long selection of music-playing apps that you can control from the watch (under Android, at least, I have 15 apps listed, including Audible, Netflix, Hulu Plus, and the standard Video Player).- Long battery life. Other devices rarely last 3 days, but the Pebble has lasted me a full 7 days before showing the low battery warningOverall, for the ability to control my phones status (silent/vibrate/normal through Phone Ringer), see notifications from any app I choose (Pebble Notifier), answer calls and mute them (PebbleDialer), or design my own watch face (Canvas for Pebble), this watch is great for the price. I DON'T need a second phone on my wrist, just a tool to see what's going on in my phone and control it a bit. Between the price and the battery life, I can live with picking and choosing which features I want and downloading those apps (for now).

reviewText: I have owned this watch for just under a year now.  Within the first two weeks of wearing it, the crystal face started accumulating scratches, which is something I have never had a problem with on any other watch--Casio, Timex, Fossil, and Tag Heuer.  In addition, the band, which is black stainless steel, has also faded and is riddled with scratched.  At $380, I certainly wasn't expecting the quality of a Tag, but with all of the advertising hype around this watch being a "Navy Seal" watch, I expected a reasonable amount of ruggedness which this watch completely lacks.  Recently, on a day when I was indoors and not doing anything Seal-like, the face cracked.  I called the authorized Luminox repair center in Rhode Island, explained my dissatisfaction and was told that the problem wouldn't be covered by warranty and that I would have to pay approximately $70 to have a new face put on.  The repair center is a third party repair center, so there was no point in arguing or getting mad at the lady who told me that it was a corporate policy of Luminox not to cover cracked glass--convenient way for Luminox to hide from dissatisfied customers.  I now have to fork over the $70 to salvage my $380 investment, but once I get it back, it will be used strictly as a dress watch.  Also, when I called the repair center and inquired about upgrading to a sapphire crystal instead of the mineral crystal (which Luminox acknowleges in the manual is soft and subject to marring) I was told that one was not available for my style of watch.  The fact that they even put a scratch-prone face on their watches when they have another option available for what appears to be approxinately $25 more speaks volumes about the company and their products.  Long story short, I am very disappointed in this watch.  Luminox makes a cheap product and, not suprisingly, doesn't stand behind it.  This will be the last Luminox watch I ever own.  If you are in the market for a rugged watch--beware.  Spring for a Tag Heuer if it won't break the budget, or if it does, Casio G-Shock's are a much better option--I have had one since 1990 and it is still running on the same battery!!

reviewText: I just received my new Luminox 3152 BO. I wanted to write an in depth review because I was not able to find such anywhere on the Internet.  Please keep in mind I have only owned this watch for a few hours. So actual reliability is something I will not touch on.This is my first Luminox watch.  But the watch had several features that intrigued me.First the watch is called a "Black Out" watch. The face of the watch is black. The Arabic numbers on the watch are also black.  This makes it hard to see the numbers under normal light conditions.  However they do have what Luminox calls "Night Vision Tubes" at each 5 minute increment. The "Night Vision Tubes" are also on the hour, minute and second hand.  During normal lighting situations, these "Night Vision Tubes appear to be white in color. In low light situations, the hour, minute, second hand and numbers 1 - 11 appear to be blue in color. The 12:00 position appears orange in color. (This helps orientate the watch in low light situations)These night vision tubes are not very bright and appear no brighter than a typical watch with illuminating hands. (The type you stick under a lamp to charge) But apparently you do not need to stick the Luminox under a light. Luminox states these Night Vision Tubes are supposed to be good for 25 years.The day calendar is at the 3:00 position and numerals are also in white.The case is made of stainless steel as well as the band. Both are black and the watch feels substantial in weight.  I am a fairly large guy and was worried that the watch band may not fit.  The watch came with all the links set at the longest position and it did just fit.The bezel rotates in one direction only. This is so if you bump the bezel,....it will show that you have less time left on your dive VS bumping and  thinking you have plenty of time left. (Seems pointless as I do not know anyone whom does not use a dive computer anymore.)The crown was the area of my concern. Once unscrewed it just did not feel well built. It felt like a decent pull and it would fall apart.  However, once the time and date are set, and the crown was screwed back down, the crown did feel secure.Setting the date and time was very basic. However my watch seemed to have a hiccup. I pulled the stem to the first stop and set the date to the day before actual date. I then pulled the stem out all the way. I had to pass the 12:00 position three times to get the date to change to the current date. (Should only have had to go past 12:00 two times at most.) I have purchased Citizen watches for the past 3 decades. The overall mechanics of this watch do not seem to have the quality of a similar Citizen watch.I suspect that the back of the watch may be the reason that this watch sells well.On the back of the watch case is engraved the navy seal trident.  This might give the "cool" mind set to the watch. And the watch might have been given away at some ceremony to some Seals. Or it might make a decent duty watch. But with no bezel cover and the "night vision tubes" glowing, (Though not much of a glow) I would expect this watch would not be used in the field.Overall this might be a cool watch. But  I paid almost $400.00 for this watch. With the mechanics of this watch feeling rather like a $100.00 watch, I would not purchase again.  I have a few days to decide whether I am going to return this watch.So I will take a few more days, before making that decision.  I will update this review if anything else come to light.UPDATE: After setting the watch precisely to my time clock at work and to my Citizen AT4007-54E on 5/18/12, I found that the watch had lost 14 seconds within 24 hours.This is a nice looking, "cool factor" watch. But for a nearly $400.00 watch, it should keep better time and the build quality should feel better. The watch has been boxed back up and will be returned to Amazon.com tomorrow.

description: The Casio PRW 3000 Watch won't cook your dinner, carry your gear, or give you a foot rub after a long hike, but it'll do just about everything else you can imagine on your next trek, backpacking trip, sailing mission, or time-traveling adventure. This little aluminum, resin, and mineral glass case packs a mind-boggling array of tech tools, from an altimeter to a barometer to a compass to a thermometer, all run by a solar-powered battery that'll last for up to seven months on a single charge. The altimeter, which measures in precise one-meter increments, has automatic and manual logging functions and can hold up to 30 records of high/low altitudes, cumulative ascent and descent, with a range from -2,300 to over 32,000 feet. That's just the beginning. The PRW 3000 has a barometer as well, which has an automatic pressure-change indicator to alert you to sudden swings, along with a pressure tendency graph and pressure differential graphic to give you a longer-term idea of what the weather's doing. To keep you on course, the compass has a graphic 16-point display for one-glance orientation, a bearing memory to keep you on route, and declination adjustment so your bearing is accurate no matter where in the world you are. We haven't even mentioned the one thing the PRW 3000's designed to do first and foremost--tell the time. It receives six atomic signals a day to ensure you're always on time, has 12- and 24-hour displays and five alarms so you never miss a mealtime, and sunset/sunrise, time zone, and calendar data. There isn't even space to discuss the stopwatch, 100m waterproofing, automatic LED, power-save function, or battery-life indicator, but trust that they're there.

reviewText: My wife suggested getting a watch like this as a gift for our 8-year old son, and it has turned out to be ideal.  Looks and functions just like the Casio I had at about the same age -- including light and timer functions (down to the hundredth of a second).  Fits his wrist well (on one of the tightest settings), so I can see how some have complained that the band is too small.  The face of the watch is just the right size -- not too big, not too small.  He loves to be able to compare his watch with all the clocks in his school.  It also helps him stay on task for specific amounts of time.  One day, he accidentally switched it to military time, which caused him some temporary panic ("It says 14:30! It's broken!"), but that became an opportunity to learn about the 24-hour clock.  Great deal on a great watch.

title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: I hate wearing a watch in the clinical setting, so I decided to buy this stethoscope watch.The pros: it's very easy to read and the red line indicating 15 seconds really simplifies things. It's also nice not to have a watch on my wrist, getting in the way and being a source of contamination.The cons: It's extremely lose on my stethoscope: I have to push it up to the fork at the top, where the tube get's thicker, to keep it in place. And despite being loose, it's very very hard to get it on. I permanently scratched the tubing trying to force it into the stiff, narrow opening.Another major con is the fact that it is SO loud. I can always hear it ticking on my shoulder and it can hear it when I'm trying to listen to heart or lung sounds!!I'm going to use a power tool to cut off the backing they provided and then I'll superglue a clip to it, so I can remove it whenever I want to. Once that is done, it'll be the product I was looking for in the first place.::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::EDIT:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::I made a discovery today that I feel I must include here, in the interest of fairness. It's extremely easy to put this watch on your stethoscope after all!!! All you need to do is slip it on over the exposed metal of your ear piece and push it down towards the 'Y'. This way, it is easy to remove when you want to use your stethoscope, but don't want to hear the ticking.
summary: Easy to read, but loose and very loud.

reviewText: I have always been interested in the coolest gadget watches and over the years I have had the pleasure of owning some great ones including one of the rare Casio Scientific calculator watches, the remote control watch as well as the Casio WristCamera Color (which I use even today)So the WristPDA was a natural progression for me. I had been interested in it since it was announced a couple of years back but the pricing (> $200) kind of held be back!. But the moment I saw the price drop on Amazon, well, I pushed the button and now I have this cool one too!First off, I should make it clear that overall I am well satisfied by this great little gadget. For the price I paid (79.99 at amazon) I think it is well worth the money!The only thing I was worried about while waiting for it to arrive was its size on my wrist (since I have a small'ish wrist, my WristCamera watch felt a little too bulky for comfortable use). Anyway I am glad to report that even though the Abacus is not small by any standards, its sleek design definitely does not feel bulky at all and it looks real nice on my wrist!!Since it is Palm OS powered, usage of this watch is quite similar to the usual Palm powered PDA's (the grayscale versions). The Font, although quite small, is crystal clear to read and I did not have difficulty in using any application. The included stylus although completely functional does feel uncomfortable if you use it for long. I recommend a full size stylus whenever possible.I was able to find and load quite a lot of standard applications onto this watch. Just look for the grayscale versions with support for Palm OS 4.x. Most of the freeware games work as well (although the ones dependent on the Hard keys on a standard PDA may need to be tweaked).The IrDA functions work well too and I was able to sync my cellphone addressbook with the WristPDA quite easily with a few clicks.The Handwriting recognition (Jot) is amazing as well. Infact it is so good and fast at recognizing NORMAL writing style, Initially I had difficulty 'unlearning' the special Grafitti style letter writing used by older PDA's. But if you are a Grafitti fan, then the wristPDA does support that mode as well.I only have 2 concerns with this watch:- The first one is the relative lack of any protection for the sensitive touch-screen face of the watch. For a normal PDA, there is an option of a case/pouch. But as a watch, the face is always exposed and there is a high probability of scratches/nicks from the elements. I now use a PDA screen protector film (cut to size) for reducing this problem.- The second one is the lack of any water resistance. Even rain is supposed to be dangerous for the watch! So be careful while singing in the shower with this watch :-)The other minor issue I have is the mandatory 2 day recharge period. But hey the watch is not doing anything in the night... might as well recharge it!But overall I think Abacus/Amazon deserves a hand in making such a great piece of equipment for a relatively affordable price.

reviewText: These boots were exactly what I was looking for.....cute, sexy, cowgirl boots to go with my costume. I had little time to prepare for an upcoming show and needed something like these.  This style is very hard to find.  These are not real leather, and sort of pricey for being made from synthetic material, but as I said, I loved the style. They arrived in a very timely manner and were packaged well.  To look at them, I was so excited.  Then the problem happened.......trying to put my damn foot into it!  I am a size 7.  The way these were cut, my heel could not get thru the bottom part of the boot to get my foot inside. the "inseam" was wayyy too small.  I fought, struggled and worked up a sweat, and finally....one foot managed to squeeze itself in.  I'm surprised that I didn't break the boot while doing so, but I was determined for these to work.  The other boot?  Forget it.......there was no way my foot would get inside.  I needed them for a show, so sending them back wasn't an option, especially when I'd have to pay for shipping.  I took them to a shoe repair and they tried stretching them for 36 hours to no avail.  The ONLY way to resolve this problem was to have him cut the entire back seam open and put in a zipper.  Now they are perfect, but this should never have happened and I ended up paying an extra 45 dollars! I contacted the seller with all the details, and while they were willing to issue a refund if I sent the boots back, they were unwilling to stand by their product and reimburse me for at least a portion of the repairs that had to be done.  Even if I went up a size, it wouldn't have helped as the foot was a perfect size 7 cut.  It was the inseam that was the problem.  I'm just warning those of you contemplating buying these boots.  You might get lucky and get a pair that are properly cut, but after reading some of these reviews, I'd suggest to keep searching elsewhere.

reviewText: First, I really love the look of this so called Wenger 73015 "Traveler Alarm" Black Dial Pocket Watch.The black face is very good looking, it has a black rubber bumper like guard built around it to absorb shocks/drops etc, water resistant to 99 Feet,beautiful stainless-steel case, it has the date function as well as a small well built leg that can pull out from the back to enable it to securely stand on a flat surface/table etc.It's built like a rock and feels like it, plus I always wanted a real "Swiss made" watch, so I bought this to hang on my waist pack/back pack/any shoulder bag.So what is the problem?The problem for me is the watch is called a "Traveler Alarm" and I bought it because it is supposed to have an "alarm".HOWEVER.... what Wenger calls an "alarm".... on this  "Traveler Alarm" can not even be called a joke at $156.94. (which is what it cost me inc. shipping)Sitting in my quiet bedroom... I have to hold the  so called "Traveler Alarm" 2 to 3 inches from my ear TO HEAR THE SOUND OF THE ALARM!I was in shock after it arrived, I set the alarm to hear it, and when it went off I thought it wasn't working.... until I held it 2-3 inches from my ear!The sound of the so called "alarm" is the tiniest "chirping" sound imaginable! I don't even think a dog could hear it! (and we know good a dogs hearing is)It's really a shame about the alarm, as I really like the watch.But if I am in an airport restaurant or bar and I need this to go off to let me know my flight is coming up... FORGET IT.At a bus or train station... FORGET IT.In the street.... FORGET IT.If I have to hold it 2-3 inches from my ear in my quiet bedroom... then what is the point of spending $156.94 for a Swiss Made "Traveler Alarm" Pocket Watch!!??Fortunately the seller SwissOutpost has a return policy.... but keeps the shipping charge and charges a "re-stocking" fee!So I'll get back my money... LESS $6.95 shipping to me... LESS $5.50 to send it back... and LESS a $10.00 "re-stocking" fee.Which obviously means I get refunded $128.49 of my original  $156.94 spent for this watch.... better than nothing.If you don't care about having a "real alarm" that is "AUDIBLE", it's a nice watch.If having an alarm that FUNCTIONS and is easily "AUDIBLE".... DON'T BUY THIS WATCH.**Update as of Sept 5th.:As a Labor day special, I just bought a Black Casio Men's AW80V-1BV World Time Ana-Digi Data Bank for $19.56 .. free two day shipping.With "3 different Daily Alarms (1 with snooze)"  YEA!!Later for Wenger Swiss "Travelers Alarm" watch.***Update as of Sept 9th. :SwissOutpost the seller/shipper has told me they no longer charge a "$10.00 re-stocking fee" on returns, I have received a complete "full refund" of $156.94 including shipping.To be fair to SwissOutpost... they shipped lightening fast, have a very courteous Cust. serv.. It's really Wenger who makes/designs the watch is where the problem comes from.
summary: If you need a "REAL" alarm function.. DON'T BUY THIS WATCH.

Think of them as sacrificial pins.  For a few bucks you can buy a whole pack of them yourself and replace them with some practice and no tools in under 5 minutes.  I got it when I was 16 and it has gone through 14 years of military service so far!  I have pictures of me in basic training wearing it. title: Suunto X-Lander Wrist-Top Computer Watch with Altimeter, Barometer, Compass, and Chronograph
description: The ultimate option for the outdoor enthusiast, the silver Suunto X-Lander wrist-top computer offers an accurate altimeter, a complete barometer, a precise electronic compass, and a multifunction sports watch in a single elegant package. Regardless of your excursion--whether it's climbing mountains, riding a muddy bike track, or skiing off piste--you need accurate, real-time information about your surroundings to pull off a successful trip. The X-Lander contributes by not only providing important data, but also keeping track of your activities so you can make rational decisions at key moments. In addition, the watch is user-friendly and solidly built, with a non-allergenic aluminum casing, a carbon-fiber back, a durable mineral crystal glass, and a water-resistant fabric strap.The built-in altimeter, which boasts a range of up to 29,500 feet, puts all 14 of the world's 8,000-plus-meter summits within the avid climber's range. Among the altimeter's functions are an altitude measurement function that lets you follow the vertical progress between stages, an automatic 24-hour memory that stores the altitude and ascent/decent rate for every hour, and an adjustable altitude alarm. Climbers will also dig the logbook function, which lets you record total and cumulative vertical ascents and descents as well as the number of runs skied.The X-Lander also displays the current barometric pressure and temperature--a must for activities in which weather plays a factor. The device automatically records barometric data for the previous four days, with the first six hours manifested in one-hour intervals and the rest in six-hour intervals. When the reference altitude is set correctly, the instrument also displays the present sea level pressure, which makes it easier to read and understand the barometric pressure at high altitudes.And few things are more important when exploring unfamiliar territory than a compass. The X-Lander's electronic compass contributes by guiding you with cardinal or half- cardinal points and a North-South arrow. The compass can also be set to track a certain bearing, which helps you follow a chosen direction. Meanwhile, the unit's declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between true North and magnetic North.In addition to the variety of outdoor functions, the X-Lander also displays normal time, with such add-ons as three daily alarms, a calendar programmed to the year 2089, a stopwatch with split-time measurement, and a countdown timer. Other features include a durable negative LCD display, a user-replaceable battery, and water-resistance to 100 feet. The X-Lander is backed by a two-year warranty on parts and labor.What's in the Box?X-Lander wrist-top computer, battery, user's manual.

reviewText: Finally got a chance to try this poncho a couple weekends ago on a day hike.  It started raining, and I pulled this poncho out quick and slipped it on over myself and my pack.  Plenty of room!  I like that the sleeves on this poncho are longer and also elastic cuffed, whereas other ponchos only have the half sleeves which still allow your forearms to get wet.  The length of this poncho is great for someone my size (6'1", 230lbs) even with a full pack on.  I was covered from head to just above my knees, and the expanded backside hangs just a bit lower but not in my way where I would trip on it.One recommendation though... before you take this poncho into the field, open it at home first and "prepare" it.  The plastic material may not be fully "cured" yet, so it tends to stick to itself from the factory.  Extra drying time before balling it up and putting it in its compression sack would probably cure that, but we as consumers can't control it.  So, take this poncho out at home and go through it carefully to fully separate it apart where it has stuck together.  It won't tear (don't be rough with it, of course) but still take your time.  I guarantee you don't want to break this out in the field without doing this step first, or you'll spend 2 minutes trying to get it on right.  Once it's prepped, it will slip on in seconds and not re-stick to itself.Folds up and then rolls up to easily fit back in the included compression sack.  Best piece of lightweight rain gear I own, and if there's even a chance of rain on a backpack trip, this comes with me.Not recommended to leave in a car or hot environment during the summer.  The material is relatively thin and I would expect that it would age after a couple years of heat exposure.  Keep it in a climate controlled environment when not needed, and get years of use out of this poncho.  A tad bit pricey for just a poncho, but the design is worth it to me.

description: Building on the success of the venerable Suunto Vector, the Suunto Core keeps you informed of conditions while you hike, bike, or camp, making it a terrific companion for outdoor enthusiasts of all stripes. What can the Suunto Core do for you? For starters, it can sense an approaching squall even when the sky looks clear. This intelligent Storm Alarm--one of several intelligent features designed to keep you safe and secure--is activated by a rapid drop in air pressure over a three-hour period. The built-in altimeter, meanwhile, displays your current elevation, shows how much you've climbed or descended, and records your entire session for later analysis. Accurate to within 30,000 feet, the altimeter is an extremely valuable tool for mountaineering, backcountry skiing, and wilderness travel. Add in such features as a barometer, a digital thermometer, a weather trend indicator, and a digital compass and you have a terrific wrist-top computer for almost all your outdoor needs. Additional features include several traditional watch functions, including dual times, a date display, and an alarm; predicted times for sunrise and sunset to help you maximize your daylight hours; an automatic Alti/Baro mode that senses movement or lack thereof and switches between the altimeter and barometer accordingly; a depth meter that provides accurate water depth readings to 30 feet; and the ability to function in English, German, French, and Spanish. reviewText: I'm addicted to this watch and let me tell you--I use and abuse it.  It's been on my wrist for 2yrs10mos; honestly I can recall less than a dozen times I've had it off.  This watch has been to Burning Man (extremely harsh conditions) and around the world (18 countries, 35 cities).  It's been on hikes and runs.  It's been submersed without abandon.  I use nearly every single function, constantly.  I have never had another sport-type watch and yet I didn't have to read the instructions in order to use it.  I find the functions very intuitive.When I say I use the functions I don't mean that I used the timer once to hard-boil some eggs.  I mean that I actually USE all the functions ALL DAY LONG.  I consult all three time zones daily because I have/had a husband in Iraq and have friends and family abroad.  I use the chrono/lap four times per day to monitor the baby's naps.  I use the timer at least six times/day for the laundry, heating bottles, and with the "repeat at end" function to remind me to drink water every two hours.  (I could use a 2nd timer, to be honest.)  I use the alarms and love that they can be set for only weekdays, only weekends, or every day.  (What a great idea!)  I use the nightlight every night since the baby is up at least once and, naturally, I open one bleary eye to check the time.  Regarding the night light I wish the light stayed on a little longer and I find the flick light function to be worthless.  You'll break bones in your wrist flicking it hard enough to make the light come on.This watch has been on the slopes and in rainstorms, pools, hot tubs, and the ocean.  It's been on my wrist for every shower I've ever taken and submersed in dishwater twice a day.  The highest compliment I can give the water-resistance feature is that I have never hesitated before doing something while wearing the watch.  I just assumed it would work and it did.  I have never had a water problem with it.I replaced the battery once, I think.  (Maybe twice?)  I haven't had the band breakage issues that others have had, possibly because I never take it off and thus never "stress" the band.  The silver paint around the face began to wear off shortly after I got it and it's looking pretty WT right about now but the plastic under the paint is sort of a metallic-ish tan/silver so it's not really too noticeable to other people unless they are really looking at my watch.  Demerits for that.The styling is definitely "sporty" and it doesn't translate well to dress clothes.  I covet those Tissot/TAG/etc metal casual watches but to be honest, I can't do without the precision chrono and timer let alone the awesomeness of never having to remember what day of the week (or month) it is because I can always just look at my wrist.  Why doesn't Timex make one of these in metal?  I don't mind the digital display, just sometimes would like something other than resin and rubber.After 2yrs10mos the band finally broke when my daughter pulled on it.  I'm ordering the exact same style and would pay ten time this much for the amount of use and functionality I got out of it.  Highly recommend.

reviewText: This is my third time buying this watch, everytime I've had to replace it... it's because I've let someone borrow it for whatver purpose adn they've lost it.There's not much to say about this watch, it's durable, it's waterproof, sorry, water RESISTANT, which just means that you can't take this watch diving, but for everything else in your life, it's fine. Cooking, showering, swimming, beach, surfing, etc. This watch can handle it, but diving is a no go.It's easy to set an alarm, use the stop-watch, set the time, etc. It's a simple watch, it's straightforward. I like it for it's smaller and slimmer profile, and the rubber band.CONS:- The backlight on the watch could better. The watch has a light but the light only comes from the leftside of the screen, it's bright enough to illuminate the entire watch face but you can clearly tell the light only comes from the left, because part of the right side of the watchface is still somewhat dim even while the backlight is on.- It'd be nice to have a dedicated light button. Sometimes I need to ajdust the time, or check the stopwatch, or shut off an alarm in the dark, but it's not possible here, because the light button is the selection button, it changes your current setting selection, so if you want to add an hour to adjust for daylights savings, you can't do it in the dark, because everytime you get your watch to the hours setting, if you push the light button, it will change to the date-settings, so you'll suddenly be forced to adjust the date. I know the slightly more expensive version of this watch has 4 buttons which gets rid of this problem, so if this is going to be ahuge problem for you, spring for 4 buttons intead of 3. It's not that big of a deal for me, but just something you might want to be aware of.

reviewText: Bought this watch two weeks ago, too early for "five year" review!!  That said, I've owned a lot of sports watches and this one may well have incorporated most of the features used by most of us some of the time!!!  Dual time, easily reviewed with one touch of "start" button in time mode!!!  Easy and very convenient, I keep second "zone" on UTC.  The clarity of the watch face is beyond expectations re: any digital watch I've ever seen.  Large digits, unbelievable contrast, have to see to believe, and programmable format to some extent.  Chronograph, with lap counter and review easy to function and access.  Timer easily activated and set with a touch of the "start" button in that mode.  Alarm functions CAN BE HEARD and the back light has to be seen to be appreciated!!!!  Also, it beeps and BLINKS at you when the alarm activates, if you fail to hit a button on the watch it will reactivate five minutes later .... pretty dern good and it works!!!!  I can't see the band on this one breaking any time soon .... it's comfortable but very substantial .... can be replaced!!!!!I don't get excited by much but this watch has been thought about by someone(s) who know something about what is going on technically and have obviously "been there" when it comes to using a "data watch" in the real world.24 hour format available, intuitive setting all modes, beeps on/off, daily, weekly, weekend alarms available, hourly alarms available (never used that myself)................... A LOT OF WATCH, FUNCTION AND USABILITY TO BE IN THE $40 DOLLAR RANGE!!!!!Now, will it endure ......... "time" will tell???????  If the submersion rating (200 meters) is even marginally correct if should last for years!!!!  One last thing, a friend of mine has one of these, has used it constantly for months and has yet to exhaust the battery ... he found out Super Wally World will replace the battery for $7.00 .... reviewText: To start off, I ordered this on a saturday evening, and received it via UPS on Tuesday around 7:00PM, and that was one-day shipping.Anyways, the watch has some really cool functions, and looks amazing. I've owned $20 watches at Walmart/Meijer stores, Rolex, Omega, and I've recently been using an iPod Nano 6 with a white Nanotch(tm) watchband. The G-Shock has a white matte finish, and if you're a student, or someone working at a cubicle and writes a lot, then it is a possibility that you could smear graphite (from the pencil or ink from pen) onto the watch, but you could wash it off with soap and water.This watch is based off timezones to calculate the time, and it comes with a manual (timezones are at the last pages). The manual is in English, Spanish, and French I think b:The hands move around based on what the digital display reads; you can turn on and off daylight saving time too. (Watch arrives in EST, NYC.) We all know that the watch is waterproof, shock-proof, anti-magnetic, so I don't really need to say anything an those topics. You can change the backlight duration from 1.5sec - 3 sec, and it is pretty cool. There's military time (24HR digital display) and the normal time (12HR) with a little PM that is in the top left corner of the left display, when it's the afternoon. It has a really accurate stopwatch, with laps and a split. (Great for running and you don't have to be worried when it rains, unless you have your phone) There's a timer, which for some reason, only goes up to 24 minutes... you can adjust the duration. (You can set it to one time run/alarm, or a constant loop until you turn it off).There are 26 world times; I have mine to London, and it works GREAT. (Takes like 2 seconds to calculate but I'm fine with that) It has 4 alarms; you press reverse or forward to stop them, a snooze (Like a wake-up alarm) and you press either reverse or forward to snooze it. Will come back on in like 3 mins, but you have to turn it off and on again to stop it.)There's an option to turn on hourly chime which beeps twice at every hour. You press reverse to turn on the backlight, and hold it down for 3 seconds to enable the auto-light when you tilt the watch 45.  The left circle on the upper half of the watch displays whether snooze, alarm, auto-light, or hourly chime is on. The middle has something to do with the stopwatch, you can see some accuracy in the timing (I guess xD) and the right circle... This I'm clueless on, but I think it also has to do with the stopwatch and stuff :).The hour nobs are "glow-in-the-dark", and, unfortunately, the hands don't have an illuminating tab on them. The lower left display shows the time in digital form, press forward and it shows the date. The bottom right screen shows the day (eg: Mon as in Monday) and below it is the seconds. (Btw the hands are SUPER precise when they point at the little lines like for example, it is 1:00 or 13:00. The hands point exactly where they should be, and when the seconds reach around 30 seconds, the minute hand moves a tiny notch! Then, when it's 1:01 or 13:01, it points normally.) The contrast on this watch is really nice; I've gotten tons of compliments... some of my friends are even jealous! This is my first G-Shock and I'm not disappointed! I LOVE the double-clasp band, doesn't seem like it will come loose, the buttons have a nice texture, and I learned how to operate this watch in about 5 minutes (I was CLUELESS when I first got it, lol) The manual helps, and I HOPE my review helped you too! Relatively fast shipping, great watch, beast looks, best $100 I spent! This watch is part of the Japan Movement, and is housed/cased in China (I don't care where it was manufactured :D) and I'm simply just impressed... the dial is pretty big, and it it looks beautiful. If you have any questions please ask! I will hopefully respond quickly :)UPDATE NOVEMBER 2013: After using this watch for more than a year (Sept 29, 2012) I can say it's still working fine! Battery life is (supposedly) 2 years... I don't have any battery problems with mine! However, the paint is starting a chip slightly. I've gone snorkeling/scuba diving, dropped it many times off high places, FROZE MY WATCH, and many more rigorous tests... this thing is a tank! Some dirt and grime is starting to build up around the strap; it has a slight brown tint from my use. I don't use auto-light at all really, and the snooze is somewhat quiet... so don't use this as a primary alarm clock!I love the stopwatch. It's so freaking usefull and goes to the thousandths of a second! (ex: 12.345 seconds) Hopefully I will post a picture on this page to show what it looks like after all this time!

reviewText: Short story:  great watch with great features (two time zones, multiple alarms, countdown timer, plus standard stopwatch, time/date)... but the band sucks and is NOT replaceable.Unlike other reviewers, I have no problems with water, even though I wear mine in the shower daily and pool a time or two per week for laps (consistently for 18 months now).  I love the countdown and repeat timers to set my pace and keep my workout moving (or cooking reminders, or naps:).  Indiglo is a bit hard to read in dim light, but lights up very well in darkness.  Buttons are easy to use and well labeled.The watch band, however, sucks.  The sides of the band, where it wraps around the face of the watch, separated after only two weeks' use.  I've re-glued it multiple times; when stretched into place, it stays (sort of), but still pops out often, which is irritating if not problematic.  After about one year of use, the small ring which holds the tail against the watch strap broke, so I'm left with a flapping band--which makes the watch fly off at the least provocation.  And the band is not replaceable, at least not locally.I like the look and function of the watch; Timex just needs to do something about the band.

reviewText: My foot has been 6 1/2 WW for many years.  Now I suffer from lymphedema, which means my feet and legs are swollen.  I have been looking at shoes and slippers to fit my feet for many years.  I bought 3 or 4 pairs of Nufoot Mary Jane Slippers in several colors, and found them to be VERY comfortable- no Velcro (I usually have to add extra Velcro to boots and shoes that use that device to get the straps to fit).  I ordered a few pairs of Nufoot Betsy Lou Slippers, but they are two-piece with a strap, and I found that the heels fell off the back of my feet, so I will return those. I bought the Mary Janes in a few more colors, so can change them to match my outfits.  They are washable, and, should I travel, will pack well.  The Mary Jane is a stretchable one-piece slipper that hugs my feet and feels very comfortable, akin to going barefoot (I just saw something on the TV program "The Doctors" about the benefits to the feet and knees of going barefoot, and they were touting a barefoot shoe- not, to my knowledge, Nufoot, but still...).  I buy the extra-large because of the extra swelling in my feet. The toe is a tad long, but is not troublesome.  I am not sure if they are long enough for women with size 11 feet, but perhaps the stretchiness will accommodate them as well.

reviewText: I LOVE these booties (and theBaffin Unisex Cush Insulated Slippers).  I got the Cush slippers last year in November and just ordered these as the soles to the Cush slippers are just starting to wear thin (although there's still a few months of life left for sure, the new ones are more to augment the old ones).They are similar to the Cush but are a taller, more adjustable, warmer and with a much thicker sole (this is good and bad.  Not quite as comfy in the house but much better insulation from the cold ground). Both are ubber comfy and very warm.  If you're going to be using them in a house that is fully/mostly carpeted I would recommend the Cush slippers, if you're going to want light use outside or for camping, or on all hardwood or other hard and colder flooring surface I would recommend the base camp booties.By the time the Cush are completely worn out they would have given me a over a year of use in a house with a mix of (some) hard wood and (mostly) carpet plus many trips out to the car and around the corner to the mailbox.  The exterior sole material on the base camp booties is the same as the cush from what I can tell, but there's an additional layer of firmer insulation in the sole of the base camp booties.  I expect these booties to last a good 18-24 months.  That may not seem like a long time but it's worth it - less toughness, more comfort.I usedKiwi Camp Dry, Heavy Duty Water Repellenton the Cush slippers and that did a great job of waterproofing them.  Not to the point where you can walk in puddles but but when I had to run outside in the snow it kept my feet dry (although the Cush slippers were, um, very slippery in the snow.  Almost ate it a few times).  I'm going to waterproof these base camp booties and I'm thinking they'll even be suitable for treading through small puddles due to the much thicker soles. I'll post back on this one.  It is summer and I don't think I'll have a lot of opportunity to use these just yet.  I bought them now because they're about $8 less than they were in the winter time.  We're going camping in a couple weeks so I report back on how they performed in the field.Like the Cush slippers, these booties run a little small (although not as much as the Cush slippers).  Here's the correct sizing chart (came with the booties and is the same sizing guidelines as the Cush slippers):Men: L = 7/8, XL = 9/10, XXL = 11/12, XXXL = 13/14Woman: S = 5/6, M = 7/8, L = 9/10, XL = 11Youth: YS = 10/11, YM = 12/13, YL = 1/2, S = 3/4, M = 5/6I would suggest ordering a size up if you're on the high end of the size if you want room for thick socks. I wear a size 10 shoe and the XL Cush fit bit they're tight with thick socks and the XL base camp booties have just a bit more room.All-in-all both are great booties and I can't recommend them highly enough!Hope this helps!

reviewText: This watch fits my small wrist very well, and I like the slip-proof feature on the loop that holds the end of the strap in place.  The watch contains useful features:  chrono, timer, up to 3 alarm settings and an occasion reminder (which I have not used).  I like the chrono feature very much and use it to time my walks everyday.  The timer is great for timing my yoga classes and meditation sessions as the alarm is relatively non-intrusive.  Style-wise, it looks sporty and 'oversized' on my wrist, which, I think, makes my wrist look more 'feminine'.  I like the black, grey and chalky light blue color combo--very classic and pleasant.  The lighted and large display (for the light, one must push a button) is easily read, though I believe Timex has a newer model that has a 'night-light' feature which doesn't depend on you pushing a button to light the display.  That would be my next watch whenever this one goes out.  The control buttons are easy to find and push, though the printing to tell what they do are tiny and barely legible to my 44 yo myopic eyes without a magnifier.  So, I've learned to memorize what each button does through repetition.  The watch is easy to use intuitively, and I highly recommend it.

description: The award-winning Suunto Core is a sophisticated outdoor instrument that gathers a range of data to help you navigate your way through the wilder parts of the world. The altimeter features a range up to 9000m (29500 ft) and sports an altitude difference measurement that allows you to track your progress in terms of altitude climbed. The log recorder stores all your movements in altitude between the start and stop times, so you can find out how much you climbed, the duration of ascents and descents, average ascent and descent speed and more. Suunto Core displays the current sea level pressure as a detailed graph, showing recording of the last 24 hours with a recording interval of 30 minutes. The storm alarm notifies you of a sudden drop in air pressure, which may be related to worsening weather conditions. Suunto Core senses your movement or lack thereof, switching between altimeter and barometer accordingly. A drop in air pressure while you’re sleeping under the stars will be recorded for what it really is: a change in barometric pressure, not altitude. The digital compass displays the cardinal or half-cardinal point and the North. The declination adjustment function allows you to correct the difference between the true North and magnetic North. The Suunto Core provides current and maximum depth reached during your snorkeling dive. The maximum depth of the device is 10m (328 ft). Watch functions include time, dual time, date, alarm, sports chronograph, countdown timer and predicted times for sunrise and sunset for over 400 locations worldwide. Also features a digital thermometer. Menu-based user interface in English, German, French and Spanish. 2 year warranty.

reviewText: When shopping for a watch, I wanted firstly a good watch. It has to keep time.I see on other pocket watch reviews, that many are subpar. They shift during movement, etc.This one, however, does not. It keeps good time and is easy to use. There is no shifting of the hands.I dropped it once, and it opened, but time wasn't affected. I don't know how good the red is, it may scratch, but it seems to be fine. Inside however, there is a spider web on the face of the clock and the second "hand" is a small spider moving (you can't see the hand). The spider web doesn't align with the numbers; the numbers are between the strands (the straight ones) but once you know that, it is simple to read. The little spider is interesting because you can't see the hand at all and it does look to be moving on its own.The chain is a little weird, but I don't use the chain so it matters not. It isn't a link chain. For a chain, it seems fine, but if you want to have a gentleman (or whatever) look, you may want to get an actual chain.Overall, the watch is good and solid. All which matters if you like spiders :)

reviewText: I'm currently suffering from light-triggered migraines as a result of a very bad concussion I experienced about a month ago (it's called "photophobia-induced migraines" and it completely sucks). Also, I have always been light-sensitive being a fair-skinned ginger so I tend to have a pretty vast collection of sunglasses/goggle that work with prescription glasses.  In-doors I've gotten away with adjusting light wattages down and wearing a pair of clip-on polarized, dark grey sunglasses over my prescription glasses (can be found on Amazon or in most dept. store sunglass section, get the spring-slider kind over the spring-wire kind as they can accomodate different widths of glasses much better).  The lense polarizing, in particular, makes reading dimmed computer screens much easier on the eyes.THIS product is NOT POLARIZED and it definitely shows in very bright condition.  I purchased these specifically for outdoor wear to cover my peripheral and brow line and they work great for that.  No longer do I have to worry about the stray sunlight or a reflection bouncing into the side of my eyes and the "ice-pick-to-the-brain" effect that comes with it.  The foam padding is comfortable and doesn't get sticky feeling even when sweating.  And the peripheral windows are great for reducing the tunnel-vision effect that other full-coverage sunglasses can have.I would recommend getting a pair of sunglass head straps for these as they do tend to slip around a lot and while fine for walking tend to require a lot of "dorky push-up" adjustment when doing anything that requires moving one's head around a lot.Even after my photophobia pass (I pray), I plan on using these when doing yard work, bicycling, and outdoor activities that involve exposure to straylight, wind and dust (really can't wait to try them on a scooter with an open-faced helmet).-1 star for the lack of polarizing and the slippage factor, but otherwise highly recommended.

reviewText: I must say before I begin this review: I was extremely ambivalent as to whether this watch is a 3 or 4 star product.As soon as I received this watch, I immediately thought it was too small, which may or may not be a good thing depending on you. I've been using my brother's G-Shock for quite a while now, and it's uncomfortable (despite all of the hype) and way too bulky! So, because of how this picture depicted the size (where the batteries go), I bought this watch. Also, the G-Shock and many other expensive watches have many designs at the sides of the back as opposed to this watch's straight round design, which makes it ergonomic. In addition, this watch is REALLY light, which again, can be good or bad. But here comes my major gripe. This watch's lighting aspect is so bad that I wouldn't even wear it if I got paid $15 to (which funnily is what happened because when I tried to refund it, Amazon politely accepted my refund AND surprised me by saying I can keep the watch too)!The light:First of all, the button for the light on this watch is so tiny which may make it hard to find for some people and also to push. But if you do manage to push the button, the light only stays on as long as you push it, and to completely kill the entire glory of the watch, the light is horrendous! I was so disappointed. Seriously, this light is so bad and only barely covers the left side of the watch. What was Casio thinking?!I would also like to add that the design of this watch is so simple and kind of boring, but once again...it's so comfortable as opposed to other bulky watches! And because of the thinness, it's much easier to slide on tight men (or women's) clothing such as dress shirts, etc. I would recommend this watch if you are willing to ignore the poorly-designed lighting portion and the ordinary look.*Unrelated*After analyzing carefully a few other inexpensive watches, I came across Casio Men's W735H-1AVCF Super Illuminator Black Watch. This watch seems really good but also uncomfortable due to the similar strap design of the G-Shock. But what makes elevated it is the huge "Light" button, which I find very important and the extremely useful vibrating alarm since I am a very forgetful person, and sometimes I may be listening to something and won't hear my watch's alarm.Also, Casio Men's WV58A-1AVCR Waveceptor Atomic Digital Watch:Has a similar designed strap (comfortable), which, as mentioned before, is what makes the Casio F91W-1 Classic Resin Strap Digital Sport Watch good! It also has EL lighting, which is far superior to LED lighting I think. Furthermore, the button for the light is medium-sized and is at the right side of the watch, which is so-so (i.e. workable).With a picky and frugal personality like mine, it's extremely difficult to find a perfect, inexpensive watch ($15-$25).

reviewText: I bought these glasses to replace some rudy project flip glasses I had been using. My hope that these being polarized and "mirror" they would be darker than the rudy project glasses I had. In reading the description and reviews I figured they would be fine but once they got here I was disappointed.The packaging was simply a plastic bag with plastic sleeves over the ear pieces. Once out of the plastic I found that I could see right through the "mirroring" from the front. I thought well maybe it is just the indoor light that is causing that. When I tried them on they end up making things brighter and not darker but the polarizing did do a good job of cutting down on the glare. I decided to give them a try for few days and I am still not happy. In full sunlight if you look just right you can see through to your eyes. To me if they are truely mirrored sunglasses you should be able to not see through the glasses from the front like you can on these. Also I find that the only thing that helps to cut the light is the polarization of the lenses. In my opinion they actually make things brighter that they normally would be.As for fit they do fit great albeit a little tight but I don't mind that as I like my glasses to stay on when I move about or bend down to pick someting up. Also when I prop them up on my head or put them on backwards when I am indoors they stay in place better than other glasses I have had in the past.I am not sure if I am going to keep them or send them back. I might keep them and look for a pair that has a truely mirrored coating since I don't want to pay for shipping and the amazon restocking fee.
summary: Don't let the picture fool you

reviewText: I like to bike for fitness as well as commuting to work during the week.  I was looking for clip-less pedals and cleats that would work for this purpose, but these aren't those.  They work well for fitness rides.  But I don't know if they would be good for riding into the city.You may say, "well, of course, why would you want to do that?"  Well, I ride over a couple larger hills on my way to work, commuting in from the Pittsburgh's South Hills area.  It would be nice to have a clip-less pedal that would reduce the load on my front quads for some of that stretch and make the ride a little easier overall.  Well the cleats on these shoes are absolutely not made for being able to walk on after you dismount, meaning you can't walk into work without changing your shoes (and yes, there are cleats you can walk on, not ideally, but these aren't even close).  Also, the locking mechanism is a little touchy.  You can make some adjustments and with practice get pretty good at it, but if you have to stop more than once every couple minutes which a commute in the city will occasionally require, then this gets cumbersome.Anyway,  I still give 4-stars, because the most common use of these shoes and pedals will be for fitness riding on more closed trail or low traffic environments with minimal stopping, and these are very good for that.  Quality could be a little better on the shoes, but it straps on nice and really isn't bad at all.  Overall makes for an improved ride over standard pedals and athletic shoes and gets me riding further and faster than I did without, which is really what these are all about anyway.So good buy for fitness uses

reviewText: Okay, you see a million reviews for this thing, so what can I add?Well, this watch does even more than the stuff which caused me to buy it in the first place!  With the right app (IFTTT) and Wemo device, this watch can turn the lights on and off in your home.  Not kidding.The primary reason I bought this is because I kept missing text messages on my Android phone.  No matter how loud I set the alert tone, and no matter what alert tone I used (including several homemade ones) I would often not hear the alert while my phone was in my holster.  Sometimes I even miss phone calls.  For complicated personal reasons, it is extremely critical that I am able to respond immediately to texts or phone calls.This watch vibrates every time I get a text, an email, or a phone call on my phone. Even when my phone is silenced, the alerts come to the watch.  And it vibrates very powerfully.  You cannot miss it.  And not only that, it displays the incoming text on the face of this watch.  How cool is that?  You can be sitting in a meeting, have your phone totally silenced, and casually glance at your watch to read an incoming text message.  There is an even an app (Glance) to send a pre-worded short response.It also displays incoming emails and the Caller ID of incoming phone calls.  You can even read your incoming email on this watch.This watch has way more applications for Android phones than it does for iPhones, which is probably a first.And then there are the watch faces.  There are a bunch of great third party sites where you can design your own watch face!  So, for example, you can download any photo or symbol or logo (whatever you can think of) and render it into a black and white watch face.  Then you can overlay an analog or digital timepiece, and overlay any text or the date (in any format).  The possibilities are endless.Use your corporate logo on a watch face and your co-workers will be putting a Pebble on their Wish List.There are zillions of really cool apps to go along with the Pebble.  An app called Glance will display the weather, show you any calendar appointments you have in the next five days, display stock information, and much more.This does have an alarm function.  It does not beep, it vibrates.You can also control your phone's music player from the Pebble.I have really pushed the envelope on this thing since I bought it a few weeks ago, and found its shortcomings.  The Pebble has a limited memory and only hold about six watch faces or apps at one time.  I also kept adding and deleting watch faces and apps so much I locked up the watch.  The "white screen of death".  I have had to reset to factory default a couple times as a result of this, and then had to reload the custom apps/watch faces.There are times, too, if you fiddle around too much, when you will have to unpair the Bluetooth connection and then pair your phone and watch back together.  There are lots of good online discussions to walk you through any problems with the Pebble you might encounter.The software has recently been upgraded to version 2.0 for the iPhone, but the 2.0 for Android is not yet released.
